statements.venue: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump, led by Sen. Van Hollen
statements.quote: a formal agreement that would slow down, and potentially enact a mutual pause in, frontier AI development to prevent cyberattacks, the development of biological weapons, and other dangerous activities that threaten the lives of the American people and humanity writ large

statements.reason: The letter she signed says frontier AI development could enable biological weapons and other activities that threaten humanity as a whole, which is level A under the threat-to-humanity ruling; a reviewer could read it as B (mass-casualty misuse) instead.

statements.quote: While advanced AI may be new, engagement between two superpowers over a technology that poses an existential threat is not.

statements.quote: The experts building frontier AI models have also been raising concerns for some time that the capabilities of AI models may soon accelerate beyond our ability to understand or control them.

record: Signed the letter from 17 Senate Democrats, led by Sen. Van Hollen, urging President Trump to negotiate an AI agreement with China, including a slowdown and a possible mutual pause in frontier AI development.
Sen. Van Hollen press release, 23 September 2026

Introduced the Workforce of the Future Act with Sens. Blunt Rochester and Schiff, requiring a study of AI's effect on jobs and authorizing education and worker training grants (about jobs, not catastrophic risk).

Her statement on the Senate Armed Services Committee's fiscal year 2027 defense bill lists AI provisions, including a review process for autonomous weapon systems and security standards for AI agents in the Defense Department (military use, not catastrophic risk).
grade_reason: The only evidence is the 23 September 2026 letter she co-signed, which calls advanced AI an existential threat and says frontier AI could enable activities that threaten humanity. No statement in her own individual words about catastrophic AI risk was found.
notes: Six web searches ran, none refused. All four statements are the words of a co-signed letter, not Hirono's own; the letter text and the signer list (which includes Mazie Hirono) were read on the Van Hollen press release page. Searches found no statement of her own on superintelligence, extinction, a pause or AI safety. No source showed her co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (coverage names only Sen. Sanders and Rep. Casar); I did not check the Congress.gov co-sponsor list. Her own remarks on AI found on hirono.senate.gov are about jobs (Workforce of the Future Act, 4 Dec 2025: "we must ensure advances enabled by AI are used to strengthen, not weaken, the workforce"), the use of AI chatbots at the Education Department (seen in search results only, page not opened), and AI-driven disinformation at a Judiciary hearing after the Maui wildfires (before 2025); all would be level D and are left out of statements. I did not find or look for a press release on her own site about the China letter.
